sources.title: First Nature fungus identification guides
sources.citation: First Nature identification guides; taxonomic notes reference the British Mycological Society GB Checklist of Fungi.

nl.summary: Rode hoed met vaak witte wratten.
nl.description: Bekende amaniet met witte plaatjes, ring en meestal een knolvormige voet met resten van de beurs.
nl.habitat: Bossen, vaak bij berk, spar en den.
nl.lookalikes: Kan worden verward met andere Amanita-soorten.

en.summary: Red cap, often with white warts.
en.description: Distinctive Amanita with white gills, a ring and typically a bulbous base with veil remnants.
en.habitat: Woodland, often associated with birch, spruce and pine.
en.lookalikes: Can be confused with other Amanita species.

de.summary: Roter Hut, häufig mit weißen Flocken.
de.description: Markanter Wulstling mit weißen Lamellen, Ring und meist knolliger Basis mit Hüllresten.
de.habitat: Wälder, häufig bei Birke, Fichte und Kiefer.
de.lookalikes: Verwechslungen mit anderen Amanita-Arten sind möglich.

nl.summary: Zeer giftige amaniet, vaak groenig met witte plaatjes.
nl.description: Heeft vrije witte plaatjes, ring en een duidelijke zakvormige beurs rond de steelbasis.
nl.habitat: Loofbossen, vaak bij eik en beuk.
nl.lookalikes: Verwarring met eetbare soorten kan dodelijk zijn.

en.summary: Deadly Amanita, often greenish with white gills.
en.description: Has free white gills, a ring and a distinct sack-like volva around the stem base.
en.habitat: Deciduous woodland, often with oak and beech.
en.lookalikes: Confusion with edible mushrooms can be fatal.

de.summary: Tödlich giftiger Wulstling, oft grünlich mit weißen Lamellen.
de.description: Weiße freie Lamellen, Ring und deutliche sackartige Volva an der Stielbasis.
de.habitat: Laubwald, häufig bei Eiche und Buche.
de.lookalikes: Verwechslungen mit Speisepilzen können tödlich enden.

nl.summary: Bruine boleet met buisjes in plaats van plaatjes.
nl.description: Stevige steel, bruine hoed en witte tot olijfkleurige poriën naarmate het vruchtlichaam ouder wordt.
nl.habitat: Bossen bij onder andere beuk, eik, spar en den.
nl.lookalikes: Diverse boleten lijken erop; controleer alle kenmerken.

en.summary: Brown bolete with pores rather than gills.
en.description: Stout stem, brown cap and pores changing from white toward olive as the fruit body ages.
en.habitat: Woodland with beech, oak, spruce and pine among other trees.
en.lookalikes: Several boletes look similar; check all characters.

de.summary: Brauner Röhrling mit Poren statt Lamellen.
de.description: Kräftiger Stiel, brauner Hut und Poren, die von weiß zu oliv wechseln können.
de.habitat: Wälder unter anderem bei Buche, Eiche, Fichte und Kiefer.
de.lookalikes: Mehrere Röhrlinge sind ähnlich; alle Merkmale prüfen.

en.summary: Yellow woodland fungus with thick, decurrent folds rather than true gills.
en.description: Usually funnel shaped with a wavy margin; the underside has thick forked folds running down the stem.
en.habitat: Mixed woodland; in Europe it is often recorded with birch and other trees.
en.lookalikes: False chanterelles and other yellow fungi can look similar; check the fertile surface carefully.

en.summary: Creamy-white grassland Agaricus with a down-turned to slightly inrolled cap margin.
en.description: Caps are typically creamy white and may develop small scales with age; cut flesh can pink slightly but should not stain yellow.
en.habitat: Grassland and meadows, sometimes in rings or scattered groups.
en.lookalikes: Other Agaricus species can be very similar; yellow-staining and other characters need checking.

en.summary: Orange milkcap with decurrent orange gills and green bruising.
en.description: Convex caps become depressed; damaged gills release orange-red latex and bruised areas can turn green.
en.habitat: Mycorrhizal in conifer woodland, particularly with pine.
en.lookalikes: Other orange milkcaps are similar and require several characters for separation.

en.summary: Variable-coloured brittlegill with unusually flexible white gills.
en.description: Caps range through violet, brown, grey, green and mixed tones; crowded whitish gills are notably pliable for a Russula.
en.habitat: Broadleaf woodland, especially with oak and beech, and also with conifers.
en.lookalikes: Many Russula species share similar cap colours, so colour alone is unreliable.

en.summary: Deadly poisonous spring fungus with an irregular red-brown brain-like cap.
en.description: The convoluted cap forms irregular hollow chambers; the pale stem is fragile and internally chambered.
en.habitat: Coniferous woodland, often on sandy soil and frequently associated with pine.
en.lookalikes: True morels have a different pitted cap structure; mistakes can be fatal.

en.summary: Brown gilled mushroom with a characteristically inrolled cap margin.
en.description: A variable brown rollrim whose gills and other tissues can darken when handled; several related species are similar.
en.habitat: Mycorrhizal with a range of trees in woodland and other tree-associated habitats.
en.lookalikes: Closely related Paxillus species can be difficult to separate macroscopically.

en.summary: Deadly poisonous small brown wood-rotting mushroom containing amatoxins.
en.description: Caps begin hemispherical and become broadly convex to almost flat; the hygrophanous surface is darker centrally and paler toward the margin.
en.habitat: Wood-rotting species found on woody substrates.
en.lookalikes: Small brown wood-growing mushrooms can be dangerously similar.

en.summary: Large parasol-shaped mushroom of grassy places and woodland edges.
en.description: A tall, large-capped species with conspicuous cap scales; mature fruit bodies have the familiar parasol profile.
en.habitat: Woodland clearings, grassy areas beside woodland, pasture, dunes and occasionally disturbed ground.
en.lookalikes: Shaggy parasols and related species can resemble it and need careful separation.

en.summary: Cream-coloured woodland fungus with teeth or spines underneath the cap.
en.description: The cap is irregular and creamy, with a fine velvety surface; the fertile underside bears downward-pointing spines rather than gills or pores.
en.habitat: Damp woodland and mixed woodland, often in groups or arcs.
en.lookalikes: Other Hydnum species can be similar; size, colour and spine attachment help separate them.

en.summary: Brown-pored bolete associated specifically with birch.
en.description: Brown cap, pale pores and a pale stem covered with dark woolly scabers; cut flesh does not rapidly turn blue.
en.lookalikes: Several Leccinum species are macroscopically similar and may require detailed study.

en.summary: Very variable Amanita whose damaged flesh reddens or pinks.
en.description: Caps vary greatly in colour and usually bear veil fragments; gills and flesh develop pink to dull-red bruising, and a fragile hanging ring is present.
en.habitat: Mycorrhizal with hardwood and conifer trees, often abundant in acidic conifer woodland.
en.lookalikes: Other Amanita species can be extremely similar; reddening is important but identification must use multiple characters.

en.summary: Thin, zoned bracket fungus growing mainly on dead hardwood.
en.description: Overlapping leathery brackets show concentric colour zones; the pale underside has many tiny pores.
en.habitat: Dead hardwood, fallen branches, stumps and standing dead trees; sometimes a weak parasite.
en.lookalikes: Zoned crust fungi can look similar but differ in the structure of the fertile underside.

en.summary: Tall white inkcap with a shaggy, initially egg-shaped cap.
en.description: Young caps are elongated and white with recurved scales, later opening and eventually deliquescing into dark ink-like material.
en.habitat: Grassland, verges, disturbed soil, parks and other nutrient-rich ground.
en.lookalikes: Other inkcaps share the deliquescing habit; cap texture and overall form help separate them.
